title: Gemini CLI crashes with `ioctl(2) failed, EBADF` in `node-pty` during `resizePty`

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue provides a detailed bug report with stack traces, environment information, reproduction details, and logs describing a crash in node-pty during PTY resizing.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: This issue involves low-level pseudo-terminal (PTY) handling via node-pty on Linux/SSH environments, which falls under Platform-Specific Complexities (PTY/Signals) and is classified as LARGE effort per guidelines.

summary.problem: Gemini CLI crashes with `ioctl(2) failed, EBADF` during PTY resize operations when running in terminal environments such as SSH.
summary.root_cause: When `ShellExecutionService.resizePty` attempts to resize a PTY process that has already closed or has an invalid file descriptor, `node-pty` throws an error (e.g. `ioctl(2) failed, EBADF`). Although `ShellExecutionService.resizePty` has error handling, unhandled exceptions propagate when `node-pty` error messages or component catch blocks do not match expected error formats.
summary.context: PTY resize operations can race with process termination or file descriptor invalidation, especially in SSH sessions on Linux hosting environments.

steps: In `packages/core/src/services/shellExecutionService.ts`, update `resizePty` error handling to safely ignore `ioctl(2) failed` and `EBADF` errors thrown by `node-pty` during resize operations on closed or invalid PTY file descriptors.

In `packages/cli/src/ui/components/messages/ShellToolMessage.tsx`, update the catch block around `ShellExecutionService.resizePty` to safely handle PTY resize errors rather than re-throwing non-matching errors.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: `ShellExecutionService.resizePty` gracefully handles `EBADF` and `ioctl(2) failed` errors during PTY resizing without throwing an exception.
verification_steps: Add a test case in `packages/core/src/services/shellExecutionService.test.ts` where `mockPtyProcess.resize` throws `new Error('ioctl(2) failed, EBADF')`.
Verify that calling `ShellExecutionService.resizePty` does not throw an exception.
